title: processkit-cli `prune --json` report
description: The single JSON object `processkit-cli prune --json` prints to stdout, in both its forms: the tally of a real reaping pass, and — under `--dry-run` — the same tally plus the `candidates` a real pass over that exact state would reap. Validate against `#/$defs/tally` or `#/$defs/dryRunReport` directly when the invocation is known. Prune deletes only entries it can *confirm* are stale: a live entry is never touched, and one whose liveness could not be probed at all is left in place rather than guessed at. A missing or empty registry is not an error — it reports an all-zero tally and exits 0. The normative prose is docs/registry.md, "Reaping — `prune`" and "Previewing a reap — `prune --dry-run`"; the in-code source of truth is src/prune.rs. Validated against fixtures/schema/cli/prune.jsonl, and against the real binary's output, by tests/machine_output.rs.

tally.description: `prune --json`'s tally of one completed reaping pass.

pruned.description: Confirmed-stale entries (`.json`/`.lock` pairs) whose files were reaped. On unix a reaped entry also takes its published private control-socket directory with it; that is counted here, not separately.

live.description: Entries left untouched because a live runner still holds their lock — paired records and lone orphaned lock files alike.

unprobed.description: Entries whose liveness could not be probed at all and were therefore left in place — liveness unknown is never read as confirmed-stale.

orphaned_locks.description: Confirmed-stale lone `.lock` files (no paired `.json`) that were reaped. Kept separate from `pruned` because reaping one deletes a single file rather than a `.json`/`.lock` pair.

dryRunReport.description: `prune --dry-run --json`'s preview: the same four tally fields — so a consumer already parsing the tally needs no new field names — plus the machine-readable list of what a real pass would reap. Nothing is deleted.

pruned.description: Confirmed-stale entries a real prune would reap.

live.description: Entries a real prune would leave untouched as live.

unprobed.description: Entries a real prune would leave in place as unprobeable.

orphaned_locks.description: Confirmed-stale orphaned `.lock` files a real prune would reap.

candidates.description: Every confirmed-stale candidate the counts above tally — exactly what a real prune pass over this same state would reap. Paired-record candidates come first, then orphaned lock files.

candidate.description: One thing a real prune would reap. Internally tagged on `kind`, so a consumer branches on one field rather than guessing which of two disjoint field sets is populated.

entryCandidate.description: A paired `.json`/`.lock` record a real prune would reap.

socket_dir.description: The private control-socket directory a real prune would reap along with this entry's two files, or null when it would reap none — the record published no endpoint, published one that is not the shape a control server creates (so the reap refuses it rather than deleting it), or is a Windows record, whose named-pipe endpoint leaves nothing on disk. Always present, so a consumer reads one field rather than inferring from its absence.

orphanedLockCandidate.description: A lone `.lock` file with no `.json` sibling a real prune would reap.

lock_file_name.description: The lock file's name, with no directory component.
